Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta )$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above)?
worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta ),$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=12\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ).
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta ))^{2}+(12\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ))^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡(4\theta )+144{cos}^{2}⁡(4\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡(4\theta )+16{cos}^{2}⁡(4\theta ))}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡(4\theta )+16{cos}^{2}⁡(4\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
